metaDescription: Group Türkiye's 22 UNESCO World Heritage Sites into smart 10–14 day loops, including Sardis, Gordion, Arslantepe, Göbeklitepe, and Hattusa.
quickAnswer: As of 2026, Türkiye holds 22 UNESCO World Heritage Sites—20 cultural and 2 mixed—following the 2025 inscription of Sardis and the Lydian Tumuli of Bin Tepe. Trying to see them all in one trip guarantees highway fatigue. Instead, group them into three geographic corridors: Western Aegean, Central Anatolia, and Upper Mesopotamia–East.

body.text: Which UNESCO sites in Türkiye are easiest to combine in 10–14 days?

A 10-to-14-day first trip comfortably links six to eight UNESCO sites along the Western & Central corridor without rushing: Historic Areas of Istanbul, Troy, Pergamon, Ephesus, Sardis, Hierapolis-Pamukkale, Aphrodisias, and Göreme–Cappadocia. Fly into Istanbul, drive south through the Aegean, and take one short domestic flight from İzmir or Denizli to Cappadocia.

According to the official [UNESCO World Heritage Centre list for Türkiye](https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/tr/), the country spans 11,500 years of human settlement—from Pre-Pottery Neolithic sanctuaries to Seljuk timber mosques. Smart pacing groups nearby sites by regional airport rather than zig-zagging across the Anatolian plateau.

body.text: If you visit six or more state-run archaeological sites within two weeks, check the [MuseumPass Türkiye E-Kart](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009) (€165 for 15 days across 350+ Ministry of Culture and Tourism museums and sites; note that night-museum entries after 19:00 are excluded).
Which recent additions (Gordion, Wooden Hypostyle Mosques, Arslantepe) are worth detours?

All four post-2020 inscriptions reward travelers willing to step off the standard Istanbul–Ephesus–Cappadocia track, led by Sardis (2025) for easy Aegean access and Arslantepe (2021) for deep prehistory. Gordion (2023) pairs effortlessly with Ankara, while the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques (2023) anchor a rewarding overland architectural drive.

items: [Sardis and the Lydian Tumuli of Bin Tepe](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1731/) (2025): Just 90 minutes east of İzmir, the Iron Age Lydian capital where coinage was invented features a monumental synagogue, bath-gymnasium, and giant royal burial mounds—an easy add-on between Ephesus and Pamukkale.

[Gordion](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1669/) (2023): An hour southwest of Ankara, the Phrygian capital preserves King Midas's alleged wooden tomb chamber inside a massive tumulus alongside citadel excavations.

[Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1694/) (2023): Five 13th–14th-century timber-pillared mosques spread across Konya (Eşrefoğlu in Beyşehir), Afyonkarahisar, Ankara (Aslanhane), Eskişehir (Sivrihisar), and Kastamonu—worth seeing individually as you cross Central Anatolia.

[Arslantepe Mound](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1622/) (2021): Outside Malatya, this 30-meter mudbrick tell preserves a 4th-millennium BCE palace complex, pre-writing administrative clay sealings, and the world's oldest known swords.

body.text: How do you plan Göbeklitepe, Nemrut and Hattusa together?

Combine [Göbekli Tepe](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1572/) and [Nemrut Dağ](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/448/) on a dedicated 5-to-7-day southeastern loop—adding Arslantepe in Malatya—and save [Hattusha](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/377/) for a separate Ankara–Cappadocia route. Driving directly from Hattusha (Çorum province) to Şanlıurfa eats an entire 9-hour day on the highway with little gain.

For the southeast, fly from Istanbul to Şanlıurfa (GNY) for Göbekli Tepe (9,600–8,200 BCE) and the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum, then drive three hours north to Kahta for sunrise or sunset among Antiochus I's colossal 1st-century BCE summit statues on Nemrut Dağ (2,150 m; accessible roughly May through October due to snow). Continue north to Malatya for Arslantepe Mound and fly back to Istanbul from Malatya (MLX), or link across to Diyarbakır.
Which sites require a specialist archaeologist guide?

Sites with intact standing marble—like Ephesus, Pamukkale, or Istanbul's mosques—read reasonably well with good preparation, whereas earthen tells, Bronze Age foundations, and Neolithic megaliths demand a licensed [TUREB specialist guide](https://www.tureb.org.tr/) with an archaeology background. Without one, Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, Hattusha, Gordion, and Arslantepe look like stone trenches and mud walls.

A specialist turns low limestone foundations at Hattusha's Great Temple and the rock reliefs of Yazılıkaya into a living Hittite empire, and decodes the animal symbolism carved onto Göbekli Tepe's T-shaped pillars. Avoid unlicensed local touts outside site gates; Turkish law requires guides to carry an official Ministry of Culture and Tourism / TUREB badge. faq.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites does Türkiye have in 2026?
faq.a: Türkiye has 22 inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Sites: 20 cultural sites and 2 mixed cultural-natural sites (Göreme–Cappadocia and Hierapolis-Pamukkale), following the 2025 addition of Sardis and the Lydian Tumuli of Bin Tepe.

faq.q: Is the MuseumPass Türkiye worth buying for a UNESCO trip?
faq.a: At €165 for 15 days, it typically pays for itself if you visit Istanbul's major state museums plus Ephesus, Pamukkale, Cappadocia's Göreme Open-Air Museum, and at least two additional archaeological sites.

faq.q: When is Mount Nemrut open for sunrise visits?
faq.a: Road access to Nemrut Dağ's summit parking area is generally clear from late April or May through late October; winter snow blocks the upper mountain road.

faq.q: Can you visit Hattusha as a day trip from Cappadocia?
faq.a: It is a long 3-hour drive each way (6 hours round-trip). Staying one night in Boğazkale or routing Hattusha between Ankara and Cappadocia is far better.

faq.q: Are all five Wooden Hypostyle Mosques open to visitors?
faq.a: Yes, they are active historic mosques. Dress modestly, remove shoes before entering, and avoid visiting during Friday noon prayers.

faq.q: Can you visit Ani and Göbekli Tepe on the same one-week trip?
faq.a: Only by using domestic flights (such as Kars to Istanbul/Ankara and onward to Şanlıurfa), as overland driving between Kars and Şanlıurfa takes over 9 hours across mountain highways.
